title: Crystal Essence — Prism and Lattice
revision: Fable proposal — 2026-10-04 batch rebalance / Crystal classification / forked tree

classification.selector: jutsu classification: the qualifying element(s), whatever the jutsu's source
classification.applies_to: matching supported tags on all Crystal jutsu
not_selectors: equipment / required bloodline item (castability gate only)
classification.off_kit_coverage: unverified (no non-bloodline jutsu catalog with effect rows in the repository)

emphasis.primary: Offense from Prismatic Focus: the Kōsai Shippū self buff (Increase Damage Given, one row, up to +10%; sustained amplification) or the Crystal Sphere and Crystal Cave exposure marks (Increase Damage Taken, two rows, up to +8%)
emphasis.secondary: Defense from Jade Lattice: Crystal Sphere Decrease Damage Taken (fortress, +10%) or Crystal Cave Reflect (retaliation, +10%)
emphasis.tertiary: No flat Damage (R1″): no Burst trait, and the kit is not strike-led (Crystal Sphere's mark sits on a jutsu with no Damage row), so Prism stays 50 EP although it is the unique A-rank strike
emphasis.rationale: Crystal Essence is a rank-A Defensive / Sustained Damage kit with eight supported rows on five tags. Its three Crystal attacks are Prism 50 and Kōsai Shippū and Crystal Cave 40 EP, all 60 AP on cooldown 7, so the tree amplifies the rows that multiply those attacks and leaves Damage alone. Prismatic Focus answers "How do I make my Crystal strikes count: sharpen my own blows or crack the enemy open for everyone?" (Shippū self buff 35 → 45%, or both exposure marks 35 → 43%). Jade Lattice answers "How do I hold my ground: endure the blows or turn them back?" (Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 35 → 45%, or Cave Reflect 40 → 50%). Each Advanced Art carries one tag; no tag is shared glue.

nodes.name: Prismatic Focus
nodes.flavor: Light bent through one facet burns where it lands and steadies the hand that aims it.
nodes.coverage_note: Kōsai Shippū self Increase Damage Given 35 → 37% and both exposure marks (Crystal Sphere single target, Crystal Cave area enemies) 35 → 37%, 2 rounds each.

nodes.name: Razor Lattice
nodes.flavor: Grown edge upon edge, the lattice hones every strike before it leaves the hand.
nodes.coverage_note: Sustained-amplification commit: Kōsai Shippū self Increase Damage Given 37 → 40% with Prismatic Focus, live for the two rounds after the 60 AP cast on the caster's later Ninjutsu hits and Crystal, Earth, Fire or element-less hits.

nodes.name: Splintered Mountain Heart
nodes.flavor: Break the mountain's heart and every splinter carries its weight into the next blow.
nodes.coverage_note: Sustained amplification, route total +10%: Kōsai Shippū self Increase Damage Given 35 → 45%, so every matching hit the caster lands on any target in the two rounds after Shippū takes ×1.45 instead of ×1.35 (≈ ×1.074); Prism stays 50 EP.

nodes.name: Flaw in the Stone
nodes.flavor: Every stone has a flaw. Find it, and the whole face waits to split.
nodes.coverage_note: Exposure commit: both marks 37 → 39% with Prismatic Focus: Crystal Sphere (single target, Ninjutsu filter, no element) and Crystal Cave (area enemies, Crystal/Earth/Fire/None), 2 rounds.

nodes.name: Break Along the Flaw
nodes.flavor: The first crack is the invitation; everything after travels the line it opened.
nodes.coverage_note: Exposure route total +8%: both marks 35 → 43%; on a doubly marked enemy a hit matching both filters takes ×1.43 × 1.43 ≈ ×2.04 instead of ×1.82 (≈ ×1.122), from the caster and allies alike.

nodes.name: Jade Lattice
nodes.flavor: Jade does not flinch. What strikes it rings, and the ringing carries back.
nodes.coverage_note: Crystal Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 35 → 37% and Crystal Cave Reflect 40 → 42% (self, 2 rounds each); both element-less, all four stat types.

nodes.name: Flawless Sphere
nodes.flavor: A sphere without seam gives a blow no edge to catch and no face to break.
nodes.coverage_note: Crystal Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 37 → 40% with Jade Lattice (self, 2 rounds after the 40 AP cast, nearly every non-pierce hit).

nodes.name: Adamant Core
nodes.flavor: What cannot be cut does not need to hurry; it waits while the enemy tires.
nodes.coverage_note: Fortress route total +10%: Crystal Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 35 → 45%, so a hit taken in the window lands at ×0.55 instead of ×0.65 (pierce excluded).

nodes.name: Light Turned Back
nodes.flavor: The cavern keeps no light for itself; it returns every spark to the one who brought it.
nodes.coverage_note: Crystal Cave Reflect 42 → 45% with Jade Lattice (pierce included, 60% cap), live 2 rounds after the 60 AP area cast.

nodes.name: Entombed in Crystal
nodes.flavor: Walls that bite: every blow thrown inside the cavern rings back to the hand that threw it.
nodes.coverage_note: Retaliation route total +10%: Crystal Cave Reflect 40 → 50%, ten points under the 60%-of-hit cap, for the two rounds after the Cave lands.

examples.name: Splintered Mountain Heart
examples.rationale: Shippū's self buff 35 → 45%: every matching hit the caster lands in the two rounds after Shippū takes ×1.45 instead of ×1.35 (≈ ×1.074), against any target, and Prism stays 50 EP. Flaw in the Stone as the fourth purchase takes both exposure marks to 39%; Jade Lattice (Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 37%, Cave Reflect 42%) is the defensive alternative.

examples.name: Break Along the Flaw
examples.rationale: Both exposure marks 35 → 43% for the two rounds after each cast (Sphere single target, Cave area enemies), amplifying every attacker's matching hits, allies included, pierce excluded; an enemy under both takes ×1.43 × 1.43 ≈ ×2.04 on a hit matching both filters (e.g. Prism), ≈ ×1.122 over the unmodified ×1.82. Shippū's self buff sits at 37%. Jade Lattice as the fourth purchase (Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 37%, Cave Reflect 42%) covers the caster while marking; Razor Lattice (Shippū 40%) is the all-offense alternative.

examples.name: Adamant Core
examples.rationale: Crystal Sphere Decrease Damage Taken 35 → 45% for the two rounds after each 40 AP cast: a hit taken in the window lands at ×0.55 instead of ×0.65 (pierce excluded; the 15% Earth passive applies last). Light Turned Back as the fourth purchase takes Cave Reflect to 45% for a pure defender; Prismatic Focus (Shippū 37%, both marks 37%) is the alternative.

examples.name: Entombed in Crystal
examples.rationale: Crystal Cave Reflect 40 → 50% for the two rounds after the Cave lands: half of each hit the caster takes (pierce included, shields bypassed, capped at 60% of the hit) returns to the attacker. Prismatic Focus as the fourth purchase gives Shippū 37% and both marks 37%; Jade Lattice leaves Sphere Decrease Damage Taken at 37%. Flawless Sphere (Decrease Damage Taken 40%) is the pure-defense alternative, though less damage taken also means less reflected.

design_notes: Final cleanup (2026-10-04): the roster pass's +2 Damage payoff on Splintered Mountain Heart is removed, so Prism stays 50 EP and Shippū and the Cave 40 EP. R1″: the traits are Defensive and Sustained Damage (no Burst), so both prongs are needed. Strike-led fails: 2 of the 3 offensive percentage rows sit on strikes (Shippū's Increase Damage Given, the Cave's mark), and Crystal Sphere's mark is on a jutsu with no Damage row. Finisher passes: Prism is the kit's unique A-rank Damage jutsu (Shippū D, the Cave B; all 60 AP). Splintered Mountain Heart now pays off Razor Lattice with +5% Increase Damage Given (sustained amplification), and Break Along the Flaw's split moves from 2/3/3 to 2/2/4 so the capstone exceeds its Hidden step. Maxima over every legal allocation: Increase Damage Given +10%, Increase Damage Taken +8%, Decrease Damage Taken +10%, Reflect +10%, no Damage.

Magnitudes follow leverage, not printed totals. Increase Damage Given has one row, but it multiplies every matching hit the caster lands on any target in the two rounds after Shippū, so it takes the one-row +10% (×1.35 → ×1.45, ≈ ×1.074; the bloodline passive multiplies last). Increase Damage Taken has two rows from two casts that amplify every attacker's matching hits and compound on a doubly marked enemy (×1.82 → ×2.04, ≈ ×1.122, against Blood-Enchanted Eyes' three-row ×1.115 and Shakunetsu Sakura's ×1.075), so it stops at +8%. Decrease Damage Taken +10% (a hit taken ×0.65 → ×0.55, ≈ ×0.846) and Reflect +10% (40 → 50% returned) each sit on one row.

Capstones stay single-tag. The kit has no sustain row, and its only defensive rows are Sphere's Decrease Damage Taken and the Cave's Reflect, one each; a mirrored rider in the Blood-Enchanted Eyes shape would make Fortress + Light Turned Back (+10% / +8%) and Retaliation + Flawless Sphere (+8% / +10%) the same two-tag build, and Decrease Damage Taken trims what Reflect returns. Any rider on Splintered Mountain Heart would be another route's tag.

Fourth purchases: Sustained amplification (01, 02, 03) adds Flaw in the Stone (marks 39%) or Jade Lattice; Exposure (01, 04, 05) Razor Lattice (Shippū 40%) or Jade Lattice; Fortress (06, 07, 08) Light Turned Back (Reflect 45%) or Prismatic Focus; Retaliation (06, 09, 10) Flawless Sphere (Decrease Damage Taken 40%) or Prismatic Focus. On a doubly marked enemy in the Shippū window, Sustained amplification + Flaw lands ×1.45 × 1.39 × 1.39 ≈ ×2.80 against Exposure + Razor's ×1.40 × 1.43 × 1.43 ≈ ×2.86 (≈ ×1.139 and ≈ ×1.164 of the unmodified kit; the latter is the tree's top offensive package, under Blood-Enchanted Eyes' ×1.234). While Shippū's window is live, Sustained amplification leads on every enemy that is not doubly marked and needs one cast; Exposure leads on a doubly marked enemy and on allies' hits, so neither dominates.

Filters and delivery: Shippū's self buff (Crystal/Earth/Fire/None, Ninjutsu filter) amplifies any Ninjutsu hit and any Crystal, Earth, Fire or element-less hit of any stat type; Sphere's mark (Ninjutsu, no element) any Ninjutsu or element-less hit; the Cave's mark Crystal, Earth, Fire or element-less hits. Shippū, Prism, the Sphere and the Cave all have cooldown 7; Shippū and the Cave are 60 AP circle spawns, Prism a 60 AP single shot, the Sphere a 40 AP single cast. Rows are live in the two rounds after their cast round, and SELF rows land on the caster at cast time once the cast has a legal target. Pierce ignores every modifier here except Reflect.
Untouched rows: the three Damage rows are unamplified; Prism's wound and the Jade summon are unsupported. Skill-tree effects and passives are skipped in RANKED_PVP and RANKED_SPARRING.
risks: Classification: Crystal is shared with Sea-Maiden's Kiss (expected under RUL-2026-10-03-005). 5 of 8 kit rows carry Crystal; Crystal Sphere's two rows and Crystal Cave's Reflect row need the proposed jutsu-classification resolver, and Crystal Sphere qualifies only through an authored Crystal jutsu classification (ENGINE_GAP_REGISTER G1). Off-kit Crystal coverage is unverified.

Exposure breadth: at +8% both marks are 43% for two rounds and amplify allies' matching hits as well as the caster's (pierce excluded); a doubly marked enemy takes ×1.43 × 1.43 ≈ ×2.04 against ×1.82 unmodified (≈ ×1.122). Team value was not simulated.

Increase Damage Given stacking: Shippū's 45% compounds with any main-tree or item Increase Damage Given, and the bloodline passive (about 28.75% at level 25) multiplies last (×1.45 × 1.29 ≈ ×1.87 in the window). The route's value depends on landing Prism or the Cave inside the two-round window.

Reflect cap and uptime: 50% leaves ten points under the 60%-of-hit cap, but main-tree or item Reflect could saturate it. Reflect pays only when the caster is hit in the two rounds after a 60 AP Cave cast, and Decrease Damage Taken active at the same time lowers what is reflected.

Friendly fire: Crystal Sphere is an OTHER_USER single cast whose mark (friendly fire none = ALL) lands on an ally if the Sphere targets one, up to 43% on the Exposure route; its Decrease Damage Taken window also needs a legal target in range 4. Prism's damage (friendly fire ALL) hits an ally it targets. Shippū's and the Cave's damage and the Cave's mark reach only enemies.
Skill-tree effects are skipped in RANKED_PVP and RANKED_SPARRING. No combat simulation was performed.

audit.revision: Fable proposal — 2026-10-04 batch rebalance / Crystal classification / forked tree
limits: Proposed element-wide potency classification; not implemented or verified in the live engine (needs a jutsu-classification resolver).

Bonuses apply to matching supported tags on all Crystal jutsu. Off-kit jutsu of the element are in scope by rule; their count is unverified. Original combat elements, recipients and stat/general/element filters stay intact.
Bloodline id, equipment, injected-child provenance and jutsu names are not selectors; equipment only gates castability.
Coverage counts below are this kit's rows only. Every matching row on a jutsu receives each matching modifier; repeated rows are counted separately.
Damage values are raw power (EP), not final-damage percentages; every other modifier is shown with %. Percentage-valued tags are capped at 100.

Afterburn is an enemy debuff: for its existing duration, damage the target takes causes extra Afterburn damage at its percentage (60% cap per hit). It is not itself a damage instance; downstream instances were not simulated.
Unsupported tags (e.g. wound, shield, stun, pierce, absorb, poison, drain, summon) receive no bonuses.
No combat simulation. Budget and numerical non-dominance checks do not establish equal combat strength.
Main-tree effects, bloodline passives, equipment, AP, uptime and modifier delivery are outside this audit.

foundation_sentences.01: How do I make my Crystal strikes count: sharpen my own blows or crack the enemy open for everyone?
foundation_sentences.06: How do I hold my ground: endure the blows or turn them back?

route_identities.03: sustained amplification: Shippū's self buff on every matching hit the caster lands in its window
route_identities.05: exposure: every matching hit on the marked target, compounding where both marks land
route_identities.10: retaliation: the Cave returns half of every blow in its window

design_review.director_review: Roster questions: DQ-B (Break Along the Flaw +8% Increase Damage Taken on 2 rows: Crystal Sphere 35 → 43%; Crystal Cave 35 → 43%; ≈ ×1.122, against Shakunetsu Sakura ×1.075 and Blood-Enchanted Eyes ×1.115).
concerns: Damage is unamplified (R1″): no Burst trait, and the strike-led prong fails (2 of 3 offensive percentage rows on strikes; Crystal Sphere's mark has no Damage row) although the finisher prong passes (Prism is the unique A-rank strike). If the director waives the strike-led prong, Splintered Mountain Heart is where a Blood-Enchanted Eyes-style +2 Damage payoff after Razor Lattice's setup would go (Prism 50 → 52).

Break Along the Flaw keeps exposure at +8% on two compounding team-wide rows (≈ ×1.122, against Blood-Enchanted Eyes' three-row ×1.115); it should move with the roster's other two-row exposure routes, not alone.

Splintered Mountain Heart is a bare +10% on one self row (≈ ×1.074). The anchors that reach +10% on one row carry a rider, but this kit has no sustain row and every candidate rider is another route's tag; the fallback is Razor Lattice +2 and the capstone +4 (route +8%, ≈ ×1.059).

Adamant Core and Entombed in Crystal are single-tag, lighter than the anchors' defensive riders; the kit has one row per defensive tag and the only riders are each other's tag or the offensive rows (design notes).

Sustained amplification + Flaw in the Stone (≈ ×1.139) and Exposure + Razor Lattice (≈ ×1.164) are close in a fully set-up Shippū window on a doubly marked enemy; Exposure leads there and on allies' hits, Sustained amplification on every other target in the window. Uptime and party play were not simulated.
Fortress, Retaliation and half of Exposure depend on Crystal Sphere's authored classification or the element-less Cave Reflect row reaching the proposed resolver (G1).
